spec.title: vscode PROP-001: The `vscode` project type - overview and module map

status.comment: the module of the vscode project type, created by the PROP-016 split of 2026-09-09; the facts moved here are the answers today's engine used to carry inline, and they keep their anchors and their statuses

p.VSCODE-TYPE-IS-AN-ANSWER-SET: `vscode` is the project type (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-016#TYPE-TERM`) that carries the tool's knowledge of the Visual Studio Code family of upstreams: where own code lives, which file is the product manifest, how a service is overridden, how the tree is built and tested, which images a distribution carries, which library the runtime capability delivers. The engine of `modules/codkit` asks the nine questions of the contract (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-016#TYPE-CONTRACT-IS-CLOSED`); this module is the set of answers, and nothing here is a fact about the engine.

p.VSCODE-TYPE-CHANGES-NOTHING: The type is today's behaviour extracted without change (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-016#TYPE-VSCODE`). Every fact of this module that carries an anchor moved here from `modules/codkit` in the specification split of PROP-016 phase P1 and moved **verbatim**, keeping its anchor, its wording and its status; the old address holds a tombstone and stays valid for citations (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-016#TYPE-SPEC-TOMBSTONES`). A fact with no tombstone behind it is new with this module and says so by its status.

p.VSCODE-MODULE-MAP: Module contents: PROP-001 the type and this map; PROP-002 tree layout - the own root, own extensions, the cleanup whitelist, the forbidden patch targets; PROP-003 layers - the `product.json` overlay with its `product.overrides.json` dev channel, the built-in extensions, the `registerSingleton` service override, the entry modules; PROP-004 build and test - the dependency install, hygiene and eslint, the watch channels and their pass boundaries, the test runners and the package build with its stamps; PROP-005 the readers of the upgrade advisory; PROP-006 the brand image set - the target table and the artwork families; PROP-007 the runtime library delivered by the `runtime-library` capability; PROP-008 the generators - the feature skeleton, the brand table and the `nls.ts` hook; PROP-009 the conventions defaults - the subsystems of intervention ids and the forbidden service ids. The contract these answer is `modules/codkit/PROP-016`; the neighbouring measurement of the upstream is `research/vscode-facts-1.135`.

p.VSCODE-CAPABILITIES: The type declares every optional capability of `spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-016#TYPE-TERM-CAPABILITY`: `brand-images`, `gen-brand`, `build-channels`, `runtime-library`, `own-extensions`, `service-override`, `entry-module`, `config-overlay`, `dev-channel`, `upgrade-advisory`. No verb of the roster refuses over a `vscode` patch set for want of a capability, which is what makes the extraction invisible to the existing product.

p.VSCODE-UPSTREAM-IDENTITY: The type's answer to the identity question (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-016#TYPE-AREA-IDENTITY`): the pin tag is an upstream release tag of the form `<major>.<minor>.<patch>` (`1.135.0`); a healthy tree carries `product.json` and `package.json` at its root and `src/vs/` below it; the origin is proved by the reachability of the anchor commit of the microsoft/vscode history, and the anchor policy is the engine's `ANCHOR-COMMIT-RULE` computed once per patch set. The resolution of a pin into `tag@sha@date` is universal and stays the engine's.
